Stacked Git (StGit)

StGit is a tool for managing Git commits as a stack of patches.

Usage

  stg <command> [options] [args]

Examples and documentation

  - Quick example and tutorial: https://stacked-git.github.io/guides/
  - Man pages and subcommand reference: https://stacked-git.github.io/man

Installation

  Prebuilt packages are available for many platforms; consult your
  platform's package repository (Homebrew, MacPorts, Debian/Ubuntu/Arch
  repositories, etc.) or the project's releases page for binary packages.

For full documentation and man pages, visit the project's website.
Installation

Prebuilt packages

  Use your platform's package manager if available. Visit the project's
  releases page for prebuilt packages.

From a package repository

  Use your distro or platform package manager (e.g., apt, dnf, pacman,
  brew) to install the stgit package if it is provided for your platform.

If no package is available, consult the project's website for up-to-date
installation instructions and binaries.

Maintain a stack of patches on top of a Git branch.

Usage: stg [OPTIONS] <command> [...]
       stg [OPTIONS] <-h|--help>
       stg --version

Patch inspection commands:
  diff   Show a diff
  files  Show files modified by a patch
  id     Print git hash of a StGit revision
  log    Display or optionally clear the stack changelog
  name   Print patch name of a StGit revision
  show   Show patch commits

Patch manipulation commands:
  edit     Edit a patch
  fold     Fold diff file into the current patch
  new      Create a new patch at top of the stack
  refresh  Incorporate worktree changes into current patch
  rename   Rename a patch
  spill    Spill changes from the topmost patch
  sync     Synchronize patches with a branch or a series

Stack inspection commands:
  email    Format and send patches as email
  export   Export patches to a directory
  next     Print the name of the next patch
  patches  Show patches that modify files
  prev     Print the name of the previous patch
  series   Display the patch series
  top      Print the name of the top patch

Stack manipulation commands:
  branch    Branch operations: switch, list, create, rename, delete, ...
  clean     Delete empty patches from the series
  commit    Finalize patches to the stack base
  delete    Delete patches
  float     Push patches to the top, even if applied
  goto      Go to patch by pushing or popping as necessary
  hide      Hide patches in the series
  import    Import patches to stack
  init      Initialize a StGit stack on a branch
  pick      Import a patch from another branch or a commit object
  pop       Pop (unapply) one or more applied patches
  pull      Pull changes from a remote repository
  push      Push (apply) one or more unapplied patches
  rebase    Move the stack base to another point in history
  redo      Undo the last undo operation
  repair    Repair stack after branch is modified with git commands
  reset     Reset the patch stack to an earlier state
  sink      Move patches deeper in the stack
  squash    Squash two or more patches into one
  uncommit  Convert regular Git commits into StGit patches
  undo      Undo the last command
  unhide    Unhide hidden patches

Administration commands:
  completion  Support for shell completions
  version     Print version information and exit

Aliases:
  add       Alias for shell command `git -C "$GIT_PREFIX" add`
  mv        Alias for shell command `git -C "$GIT_PREFIX" mv`

  rm        Alias for shell command `git -C "$GIT_PREFIX" rm`
  status    Alias for shell command `git status -s`

          Run as if stg was started in '<path>' instead of the current working

          This option affects arguments that expect path names or path specs in that

Initialize a StGit stack on a branch.

Initializing a branch with a StGit stack commits initial, empty stack state for the
branch to the repository. Theses stack metadata commits are tracked by the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` reference. Updated stack state is committed by each StGit command
that modifies the stack. StGit users do not have to do anything with the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` ref directly.

Some StGit commands, such as `stg new` and `stg uncommit`, will automatically initialize
the stack, so it is often not necessary to explicitly initialize the stack on a branch.
Also, branches created with `stg branch --create` are automatically initialized.

The branch must already exist and point to a commit before initializing a StGit stack.

StGit stack metadata can be deinitialized from a branch using `stg branch --cleanup`.
See 'stg branch' for more details.

Create a new, empty patch on the current stack. The new patch is created on top of the
currently applied patches, and is made the new top of the stack. Uncommitted changes in
the work tree are not included in the patch -- that is handled by stg-refresh.

The given patch name must be unique in the stack. If no name is given, one is generated
from the first line of the patch's commit message.

Patch names follow the rules for Git references with the additional constraint that
patch names may not contain the '/' character. See git-check-ref-format(1) for details.

Patch names may start with a leading '-'. When specifying such a patch name on the
command line, the leading '-' may be escaped with a single backslash as in
'\-patch-name' to disambiguate the patch name from command line options.

An editor will be launched to edit the commit message to be used for the patch, unless
the '--message' flag already specified one. The 'patchdescr.tmpl' template file (if
available) is used to pre-fill the editor.

---refresh details---
Include the latest work tree and index changes in the current patch. This command
generates a new git commit object for the patch; the old commit is no longer visible.

Refresh will warn if the index is dirty, and require use of either the '--index' or
'--force' options to override this check. This is to prevent accidental full refresh
when only some changes were staged using git add interactive mode.

You may optionally list one or more files or directories relative to the current working
directory; if you do, only matching files will be updated.

Behind the scenes, stg refresh first creates a new temporary patch with your updates,
and then merges that patch into the patch you asked to have refreshed. If you asked to
refresh a patch other than the topmost patch, there can be conflicts; in that case, the
temporary patch will be left for you to take care of, for example with stg squash.

The creation of the temporary patch is recorded in a separate entry in the patch stack
log; this means that one undo step will undo the merge between the other patch and the
temp patch, and two undo steps will additionally get rid of the temp patch.

Usage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...

Arguments:
  [path]...
          Only refresh files matching path

Options:
      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Refresh Options:
  -u, --update
          Only update the current patch files

  -i, --index
          Instead of setting the patch top to the current contents of the worktree, set
          it to the current contents of the index.

  -F, --force
          Instead of warning the user when some work has already been staged (such as
          with git add interactive mode) force a full refresh.

      --conflicts[=<policy>]
          Either "allow" or "disallow" pushing a patch with conflicts.
          
          Using `--conflicts=allow` (or just `--conflicts`) allows pushing a patch that
          may result in unresolved merge conflicts. The patch will be pushed and files
          with conflicts will be left with conflict markers to be resolved manually; or
          the operation undone with `stg undo --hard`. This is the default behavior and
          also corresponds to the "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" variable being set to
          "true".
          
          Using `--conflicts=disallow` disallows pushing any patch that would result in
          merge conflicts. The operation will stop on the last patch that can be pushed
          without conflicts. This behavior can be configured by setting
          "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" to "false".

  -p, --patch <patch>
          Refresh (applied) <patch> instead of the top patch

  -a, --annotate <note>
          Annotate the patch log entry with <note>

      --submodules
          Include submodules in patch content

      --no-submodules
          Exclude submodules in patch content

Patch Edit Options:
  -e, --edit
          Invoke editor for patch description

  -d, --diff
          Show diff when editing patch description

  -m, --message <message>
          Use message instead of invoking the editor

  -f, --file <path>
          Use the contents of file instead of invoking the editor. Use "-" to read from
          stdin.

      --no-verify
          Disable commit-msg hook

  -s, --signoff[=<value>]
          Add "Signed-off-by" message trailer.

---commit semantics---
Finalize one or more patches into the base of the current stack and remove them from the
series. This is the opposite of 'stg uncommit'. Use this command when a patch is
completed and no longer needs to be managed with StGit.

By default, the bottommost patch is committed. If patch names are given, the stack is
rearranged so that those patches are at the bottom, and then they are committed.

The -n/--number option specifies the number of applied patches to commit (counting from
the bottom of the stack). If -a/--all is given, all applied patches are committed.

Usage: stg commit [OPTIONS] [patch]...
       stg commit [OPTIONS] -n <number>
       stg commit [OPTIONS] --all

Arguments:
  [patch]...
          Patches to commit

Options:
  -n, --number <number>
          Commit the specified number of applied patches

  -a, --all
          Commit all applied patches

      --allow-empty
          Allow empty patches to be committed

      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a

patches are exported by default.

Patches are exported to 'patches-<branch>' by default. The '--dir' option may be used to
specify a different output directory.

The patch file output may be customized via a template file found at
"$GIT_DIR/patchexport.tmpl", "~/.stgit/templates/patchexport.tmpl", or
"$(prefix)/share/stgit/templates". The following variables are supported in the template
file:

Squash two or more patches, creating one patch with their combined changes.

The squash process, at a high level:

    """Jaro-Winkler similarity for human-facing spelling suggestions."""

def message_template(name,author,message):
    ident,stamp=author.rsplit(' ',2)[0], ' '.join(author.rsplit(' ',2)[-2:])
    return ('Patch:  '+(name or '')+'\nAuthor: '+ident+'\nDate:   '+display_date(stamp)+'\n\n'+message.rstrip('\n')+
            "\n\n# Please enter the message for your patch. Lines starting with\n"
            "# '#' will be ignored. An empty message aborts the new patch.\n"
            "# The patch name and author information may also be modified.\n")


def prepare_message(s,opts,name=None,old=None,default='',editor=False):
    g=s.g
    author=old['author'] if old else g.identity('author')+' '+signature_time()
    ident,stamp=author.rsplit(' ',2)[0], ' '.join(author.rsplit(' ',2)[-2:])
    m=re.fullmatch(r'(.*) <(.*)>',ident)
    an,ae=m.groups() if m else (ident,'')
    if opts.get('author'):
        an,ae=re.fullmatch(r'(.*?)\s*<([^<>]*)>',opts.get('author')).groups();an=an.strip()
    an=opts.get('authname',an);ae=opts.get('authemail',ae)
    stamp=opts.get('authdate',stamp)
    author=an+' <'+ae+'> '+stamp
    msg=old['message'] if old else default
    if opts.get('message') is not None:
        msg=opts.get('message')
    elif opts.get('file') is not None:
        filename=opts.get('file')
        try:msg=sys.stdin.read() if filename=='-' else Path(filename).read_text(errors='surrogateescape')
        except OSError as e:fail('No such file or directory (os error 2)' if e.errno==2 else str(e))
    msg=g.raw('stripspace',input=msg)
    if opts.get('save-template') is not None:
        text=message_template(name,author,msg)
        dest=opts.get('save-template')
        if dest=='-':out(text)
        else:Path(dest).write_text(text)
        return None,author,name
    if opts.get('edit') or (editor and opts.get('message') is None and opts.get('file') is None):
        template=message_template(name,author,msg)
        fd,fn=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='stgit-edit-',suffix='.txt',dir=g.dir)
        os.close(fd);Path(fn).write_text(template)
        edit=os.environ.get('GIT_EDITOR') or g.config('core.editor') or os.environ.get('VISUAL') or os.environ.get('EDITOR') or 'vi'
        err('hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...\n')
        try:
            p=subprocess.run(edit+' '+shlex.quote(fn),shell=True)
            if p.returncode:fail('editor exited with non-zero status')
            text=Path(fn).read_text(errors='surrogateescape')
        finally:
            try:os.unlink(fn)
            except OSError:pass
        text='\n'.join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith('#'))
        body=[];headers=True
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if headers:
                if line.startswith('Patch:'):
                    val=line[6:].strip();name=val or name
                elif line.startswith('Author:'):
                    val=line[7:].strip()
                    if val:ident=val;author=ident+' '+stamp
                elif line.startswith('Date:'):
                    val=line[5:].strip()
                    if val:stamp=parse_date(val);author=author.rsplit(' ',2)[0]+' '+stamp
                elif not line:headers=False
                else:headers=False;body.append(line)
            else:body.append(line)
        msg=g.raw('stripspace',input='\n'.join(body))

linkstg:prev[]::
    Print the name of the previous patch
linkstg:series[]::
    Display the patch series
linkstg:top[]::
    Print the name of the top patch

Stack Manipulation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

linkstg:branch[]::
    Branch operations: switch, list, create, rename, delete, ...
linkstg:clean[]::
    Delete empty patches from the series
linkstg:commit[]::
    Finalize patches to the stack base
linkstg:delete[]::
    Delete patches
linkstg:float[]::
    Push patches to the top, even if applied
linkstg:goto[]::
    Go to patch by pushing or popping as necessary
linkstg:hide[]::
    Hide patches in the series
linkstg:import[]::
    Import patches to stack
linkstg:init[]::
    Initialize a StGit stack on a branch
linkstg:pick[]::
    Import a patch from another branch or a commit object
linkstg:pop[]::
    Pop (unapply) one or more applied patches
linkstg:pull[]::
    Pull changes from a remote repository
linkstg:push[]::
    Push (apply) one or more unapplied patches
linkstg:rebase[]::
    Move the stack base to another point in history
linkstg:redo[]::
    Undo the last undo operation
linkstg:repair[]::
    Repair stack after branch is modified with git commands
linkstg:reset[]::
    Reset the patch stack to an earlier state
linkstg:sink[]::
    Move patches deeper in the stack
linkstg:squash[]::
    Squash two or more patches into one
linkstg:uncommit[]::
    Convert regular Git commits into StGit patches
linkstg:undo[]::
    Undo

"""Black-box integration tests for the independently implemented patch manager."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BINARY = str(Path(os.environ.get('STG_BIN', ROOT / 'executable')).resolve())


class StackTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='patch-stack-test-')
        self.repo = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.env = os.environ.copy()
        self.env.update(GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Test User', GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='test@example.com',
                        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Test User', GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='test@example.com',
                        GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2000-01-01T00:00:00+0000',
                        GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2000-01-01T00:00:00+0000',
                        GIT_EDITOR='true', GIT_PAGER='cat', PAGER='cat', LC_ALL='C')
        self.git('init', '-q', '-b', 'master')
        self.git('config', 'user.name', 'Test User')
        self.git('config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com')
        self.write('base', 'base\n')
        self.git('add', 'base')
        self.git('commit', '-qm', 'Initial')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def git(self, *args):
        p = subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env,
                           text=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
        return p.stdout

    def run_stg(self, *args, code=0, input=None):
        p = subprocess.run([BINARY, *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env, input=input,
                           text=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, code, f'{args}: {p.stdout}{p.stderr}')
        return p

    def stg(self, *args, **kw):
        return self.run_stg(*args, **kw).stdout

    def write(self, name, text):
        path = self.repo / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(text)

    def patch(self, name, contents=None):
        self.stg('new', name, '-m', name.capitalize())
        if contents is not None:
            self.write(name, contents)
            self.git('add', name)
            self.stg('refresh')

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.stg('version', '--short'), 'stg 2.5.5\n')
        self.assertIn('Usage: stg new', self.stg('new', '--help'))
        p = self.run_stg(code=1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, '')
        self.assertIn('Maintain a stack', p.stderr)
        self.assertIn('\x1b[', self.stg('--color=always', '--help'))

    def test_initialization(self):

# Patch stack manager

An independent implementation of the documented StGit command-line interface,
using Python's standard library and Git's public repository plumbing.

## Build

```sh
./compile.sh
./executable --help
```

The build produces a self-contained Python executable archive in the workspace
root. It requires Python 3 and Git, with no project-specific packages or network
access. Build products, caches, and local observation files are ignored by Git.

## Implementation

`src/__main__.py` implements command-line parsing, revision and patch-range
resolution, patch editing and refresh, stack transformations, branches,
transaction history, merges and conflict handling, imports, exports, and email
formatting. Stack metadata and patch references are stored as ordinary Git
objects and refs. Git itself is used only for general repository operations;
the implementation does not invoke an existing patch-stack manager.

`src/help.json` supplies the interface text resources used for help, shell
completion output, and generated manual pages.

## Tests

After building:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The tests create isolated repositories and exercise stack operations, filesystem
and index effects, conflicts, undo/redo, branch cloning, export/import, CLI
resources, and metadata references.
